items.claim: The row's own digit-bearing sweep for its central structuring device undercounts the device it cites as evidence for holding the whole span as one developing unit.
items.evidence: The rationale states "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא" (oshb:Isa.19.16, byte tier) "recurs four further times through the row's own span (sweep: 5 sites)", but the phrase is byte-identical within this row's own span at oshb:Isa.19.16, oshb:Isa.19.18, oshb:Isa.19.19, oshb:Isa.19.21, oshb:Isa.19.23, and oshb:Isa.19.24 -- six sites, not five. The mid-verse occurrence at oshb:Isa.19.21 ("וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶת יְהוָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא") is omitted from the count. The extra site does not weaken the row's unity argument (if anything it strengthens it), but a universal/count claim this central to the row's own warrant names the wrong number.

items.claim: The row correctly holds the sign-act narration as one unit bounded by its own narrative frame and honestly discloses the operative-category deviation for labeling continuous third-person narration as vision_report.
items.evidence: The unit opens on an unambiguous fresh narrative onset ("בִּשְׁנַ֨ת בֹּ֤א תַרְתָּן֙", oshb:Isa.20.1) with no addressee or frame-device seam before the interpretive close at Isa.20.6, and the named referent ("עַבְדִּ֥י יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ", oshb:Isa.20.3) is correctly kept distinct from the book's unnamed servant-figure zones. The single-witness parashah disclosure (preceding at Isa.19.25, mid-span at Isa.20.2, closing at Isa.20.6) matches the marks inventory exactly for this span.

items.claim: The low-confidence, frontier-flagged treatment of the watchman vision is appropriately calibrated, and the row's rejected alternative honestly engages the genuine internal rival rather than a strawman.
items.evidence: No addressee or frame-device shift separates the banquet scene, the commissioning ("כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י", oshb:Isa.21.6), and the watchman's own report before the fresh Dumah header at Isa.21.11 closes the unit; this matches the book strategy's own listing of this span as a vision_report example. The single-witness parashah disclosure (setumah preceding at Isa.20.6, petuchah mid-span at Isa.21.5, setumah closing at Isa.21.10) is accurate and symmetric for the marks present in this span.

items.claim: The two-verse Dumah oracle is cleanly bracketed by its own header and the following header, and the repeated watchman question is quoted accurately at the byte tier.
items.evidence: "שֹׁמֵר֙ מַה מִלַּ֔יְלָה שֹׁמֵ֖ר מַה מִלֵּֽיל" (oshb:Isa.21.11) is byte-identical to the row's citation; the unit closes before a fresh massa header opens the following Arabia oracle, and the single-witness parashah disclosure (setumah at Isa.21.10 and Isa.21.12) is accurate.

items.claim: The row's own span, from the Arabia header through the fugitive scene, is internally coherent, and its quotes and parashah disclosure are accurate.
items.evidence: The header and scene material at oshb:Isa.21.13 and oshb:Isa.21.14 form one continuous description with no addressee shift of their own inside the row, and the single-witness parashah disclosure (setumah preceding at Isa.21.12, closing at Isa.21.15) is accurate.

items.claim: The row treats a mid-oracle divine-frame formula as sufficient to open a fresh row, while the immediately preceding row in this same part treats the same device-class occurrence as carrying no such cutting force, and the row does not reconcile the two treatments even though its own rationale names the parallel.
items.evidence: The formula opening this row, "כִּי כֹ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֲדֹנָ֖י אֵלָ֑י" (oshb:Isa.21.16), and "כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י" (oshb:Isa.21.6) are the same divine-frame construction (word order aside; both verses are tallied together as divine-frame sites, not royal-messenger). The watchman-vision row keeps its own occurrence of that construction internal to one unbroken unit and argues its rejected split lacks 'an addressee or frame-device shift in the bytes' -- a description that applies equally at oshb:Isa.21.16, where no addressee shift accompanies the formula either. This row's disclosed alternative addresses only 'keeping the whole Arabia oracle as one span,' not why the identical device-class functions as a seam here but not at the earlier site.

items.claim: The row's stated warrant for stopping at Isa.22.11 rests on a factually incorrect claim that the frame opening the next unit is absent from this row's own span, when the identical phrase occurs within the row itself.
items.evidence: The rationale states the frame opening the next unit is 'not present anywhere in this row's own span,' but 'in that day' collates byte-identical within this row at oshb:Isa.22.8 ("וַתַּבֵּט֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אֶל נֶ֖שֶׁק בֵּ֥ית הַיָּֽעַר"), rendered in the staged WEB text as “you looked in that day to the armor in the house of the forest” (web:Isa.22.8). The boundary at Isa.22.11|Isa.22.12 may still be defensible on other grounds (the fresh divine-summons verb and the shift from siege narration to a citation formula), but the row's own stated evidence for why the following verse's frame is distinctive is contradicted by the bytes of its own span.

items.claim: The row correctly brackets the mourning-summons sub-unit between its opening divine-summons verb and its closing amar-plus-title citation, and its quotes collate accurately against the staged WEB text.
items.evidence: "וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" (oshb:Isa.22.12) and the closing "אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת" (oshb:Isa.22.14) form a genuine title-bracket distinct from the preceding row's own material, and the paseq/petuchah disclosure (paseq at Isa.22.13, petuchah closing at Isa.22.14) matches the marks inventory for this span.
